name: Field-tuned damping
description: Ringing tank's circuit, its resistor now Magnetoresistance's short wide strip, in your solenoid. With no field the strip barely resists, and across the tank it shorts the ringing out: the end hardly swings after the step to 10 at $t = 5$. In a field its carriers' paths bend and it resists more, and the tank rings longer: the field sets the tank's Q, whichever way it points. Make the ringing's amplitude between 2.15 and 3 (at the period 20, over three periods from $t = 5$ to $65$). The strip's own thermal noise rings the tank too, more the longer it rings.

reality.represents: A tuned circuit whose Q a magnetic field sets

remarks.detail: The magnetoresistor across the tank resists more in a field, so less of the tank's energy leaks into it each swing: InSb field plates served as contactless, field-driven variable resistors.
The wide strip's contacts short out its Hall field, its carriers' paths bend, and it resists more in either field direction.
The strip's thermal noise drives the tank at its own frequency; the higher its Q, the more of that noise it collects there, as in every tuned circuit.
The coil and the capacitor are ideal lumped parts with no losses of their own; only the strip damps the tank.

remarks.line: A classical metal, a semiconductor by its ratios
remarks.detail: The carriers are classical particles at the lattice's temperature bouncing off fixed ion cores (the Drude model). A real metal's electrons are a degenerate quantum gas whose own ratios (plasma oscillations per collision, screening per free path) the model cannot afford; its carriers have a lightly doped semiconductor's ratios (the Scales section names which), which conducts by the same laws.

The strip is infinitely long along z, its carriers lines of charge moving as one: currents are per unit length, and the noise is larger than a real conductor's, whose carriers move independently along its length.

electrodes.label: wide strip, left contact (the tank's node: the coil from the step, the capacitor to ground)

metals.label: short wide strip (magnetoresistive, the tank's resistor)
